questions.question_text: Rewrite $\operatorname{cosec} 52^{\circ}$ as the secant of an acute angle.

options.why: Replaced cosecant with secant without subtracting the angle from $90^{\circ}$.
Subtracted from $90^{\circ}$ but kept the original cosecant ratio instead of swapping to secant.
Subtracted from $180^{\circ}$ instead of using the complementary angle sum of $90^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: Rewrite $\cot 41^{\circ}$ as the tangent of an acute angle.

options.why: Subtracted the angle from $180^{\circ}$ rather than $90^{\circ}$, giving $139^{\circ}$.
Found the complement $49^{\circ}$ but forgot to swap cotangent to tangent.
Made both slips: used $180^{\circ}-41^{\circ}$ and also left the ratio as cotangent.
Evaluated only the first quotient and omitted the subtraction of the second quotient.
Added the two quotients instead of subtracting the second from the first.
Omitted the first quotient and kept only the negative of the second quotient, giving $-1$.
Assumed numerator and denominator are equal without converting both cofunctions.
Inverted the cofunction substitutions for numerator and denominator.

questions.question_text: Find the value of acute angle $\theta$ in degrees if $\cot(3\theta+12^{\circ}) = \tan(2\theta+18^{\circ})$, where both trigonometric arguments are acute.

options.why: Set $3\theta+12^{\circ} = 2\theta+18^{\circ}$ instead of equating their sum to $90^{\circ}$.
Dropped both constants from $5\theta+30^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$ and solved $5\theta=90^{\circ}$.
Equated the sum of the angles to $180^{\circ}$, giving $5\theta+30^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$ and $\theta=30^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: Find the value of acute angle $y$ in degrees if $\sec(4y-10^{\circ}) = \operatorname{cosec}(y+25^{\circ})$, where both trigonometric arguments are acute.

options.why: Set the arguments equal, giving $4y-10^{\circ}=y+25^{\circ}$ and $3y=35^{\circ}$.
Added $15^{\circ}$ to $90^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting, giving $5y=105^{\circ}$ and $y=21^{\circ}$.
Used a supplementary angle sum of $180^{\circ}$ instead of complementary $90^{\circ}$.
Ignored the complementary arguments and used $\cos\theta/\sin\theta$.
Replaced both numerator and denominator with $\sin\theta$ instead of converting the denominator to $\cos\theta$.
Converted the numerator to $\sin\theta$ but omitted the denominator $\cos\theta$.

questions.question_text: Solve $\sec(2x+15^{\circ}) = \operatorname{cosec}(x+30^{\circ})$, where both trigonometric arguments are acute.

options.why: Found $3x=45^{\circ}$ but omitted division by $3$.
Omitted the constant $45^{\circ}$ from the complementary-sum equation and solved $3x=90^{\circ}$.
Reversed the subtraction when isolating $3x$, giving $3x=45^{\circ}-90^{\circ}=-45^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Since both arguments are acute, they are complementary.
$(2x+15^{\circ}) + (x+30^{\circ}) = 90^{\circ}$
$3x + 45^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$3x = 45^{\circ}$
$x = 15^{\circ}$
